fact_checks.observation: The Summary advances through Model I, Model II, and Model III, then adds scalability and sensitivity in a final paragraph.
The source reports an average prediction uncertainty of 2.39 percent.
The paper explicitly labels the four requirements Locate, Prepare, Search, and Extrapolate.
Figure 1 places data, trajectory, equipment, search, transfer, and memo outputs in one visible chain.
Each numbered assumption is followed immediately by an Explanation sentence.
The paper uses CMEMS current data and local coordinate conversion before forecasting and trajectory construction.
ARIMA is presented through differencing, AR, MA, and combined equations before a prediction-versus-real plot.
Monte Carlo samples are passed through ARIMA and summarized by relative residual formulas.
Ridge regression supplies location-dependent current velocity and seawater density values.
Gravity, buoyancy, resistance, current direction, and submersible orientation are introduced before the Newton equations.
The visually checked example begins near (9264, 6207, -3767) and reaches about (10342, 5554, -4062) after three hours.
The source compares side-scan sonar, passive locator, optical imaging, acoustic-beacon, and remotely operated support equipment.
Cost, availability, and readiness are defined as the three equipment-allocation objectives.
A genetic algorithm produces a Pareto front and continuous candidate solutions before later culling and rounding.
Scheme 1 selects all five equipment categories, with readiness 8, availability 9,005,000, and cost 215,000.
Scheme 2 selects optical imaging only, with readiness 0.5, availability 1,293,333, and cost 50,000.
Scheme 3 selects passive locator plus optical imaging, with readiness 1.1, availability 2,873,333, and cost 65,000.
Scheme 4 selects side-scan sonar, passive locator, and optical imaging, with readiness 4, availability 4,080,000, and cost 150,000.
The paper compares four standard patterns and then discretizes the region into probability-ranked grids.
A Poisson distribution indexed by Manhattan distance supplies the evolving spatial prior.
The worked search example uses t0=20 minutes, a 30-minute update interval, m=0.2, and n=10.
The source reports cumulative finding probability 0.5504 after five hours and 0.7160 after fifty hours.
The Caribbean example uses an east-to-west current trend as a qualitative transfer check.
Three submersibles are treated separately under independent and equal search assumptions.
The source claims a final-probability change below 5.8 percent when the search interval changes by less than 10 percent.
The memo occupies exactly two PDF pages and mirrors the four official task labels as headings.
The memo ends with an approval request after direct deployment recommendations.

g7_warnings.warning: The PDF contains a red diagonal watermark and a bottom QR/Chinese watermark; extracted mojibake must not be treated as English paper content.
The statement of 38 incidents relies on Wikipedia and is not backed by a frozen incident dataset.
The assumption that ocean currents are periodic is strong and is not tested against the selected data.
The fixed dimensions, mass, and volume used in the trajectory example are not sourced.
Simultaneously losing propulsion and volume control excludes partial-failure modes relevant to location uncertainty.
The seabed-or-neutral-buoyancy premise conflicts with the simulated descent and excludes transient positive or negative buoyancy states.
Detection whenever vessel and target share latitude and longitude ignores depth, sensor range, attenuation, terrain shadow, and false negatives.
The seven-dimensional current dataset, coordinate subset, time span, depth levels, and transformations are not reproducibly frozen.
ARIMA order, train-test split, stationarity test, hyperparameter selection, and residual diagnostics are absent.
Figure 3 is interpreted visually without numerical held-out forecast metrics.
The normal random input is not linked to a fitted residual distribution or temporal and spatial correlation structure.
The uncertainty ratio is defined with absolute values while Figure 4 displays negative uncertainty values.
The paper shifts between maximum relative error and an average uncertainty of 2.39 percent without a fully specified aggregation convention.
The ridge penalty coefficient, feature basis, training set, cross-validation, and spatial-depth domain are not reported.
Only a few predicted samples are tabulated; regression error and held-out validation are absent.
Hydrodynamic resistance should depend on relative water-submersible velocity and direction, which the force model does not fully reconcile.
Equation 18 prints the same cosine resistance component in both horizontal equations, suggesting a sine-cosine transcription or model error.
Angle definitions, sign conventions, seabed and surface contact, and collision behavior are not fully defined.
The trajectory solver, software, step size, current interpolation, parameter values, and initial-condition construction are absent.
Coordinate signs and digits are corrupted in extracted text; exact trajectory values must be anchored to the source visual.
The three-hour point estimate has no propagated uncertainty band despite the preceding 2.39 percent current-forecast claim.
Communication ranges, depth ratings, costs, maintenance, readiness, compatibility, and product sources are not frozen.
Range divided by sensitivity is dimensionally and semantically unclear, and multiplying six raw coefficients produces an unnormalized score.
Table 6 averages products or models without preserving product-level provenance or uncertainty.
The maintenance-cost-over-usage term is not tied to a consistent annual or mission time basis.
The equipment decision is described as purchase yes-no in one place and as a quantity in another.
The readiness objective is actually preparation time, so lower values are better even though the prose sometimes treats readiness as a positive score.
Population, generations, bounds, crossover, mutation, seed, convergence, and repeated-run stability are absent.
The displayed front is nearly linear and is not accompanied by dominance, crowding, or robustness diagnostics.
Culling and rounding continuous genetic-algorithm outputs can destroy Pareto optimality, but the four integer schemes are not re-evaluated.
The final four schemes are chosen subjectively without a decision rule for host versus rescue vessels, capacity, budget, compatibility, or redundancy.
The recommended 1+n rescue arrangement leaves n undefined.
Equation 27 mixes vessel speed, search time, sweep width, turns, and overlap in a dimensionally unclear equality.
The 300 m by 300 m grid is not reconciled with sensor footprint, depth, bathymetry, topography, or track overlap.
A Poisson law over Manhattan-distance rings is ad hoc and lacks calibration, domain truncation, and normalization proof.
The rule lambda=m+ln(t/t0) is asserted from a probability-time ratio without derivation or calibration.
The update advances target uncertainty but does not explicitly couple rescue-vessel relocation with moving-target dynamics.
Searched cells are set permanently to zero even though a moving target can later enter them.
The prose describes the denominator using searched-grid probability even though a no-detection event requires remaining or unsearched probability mass.
Accumulated finding probability assumes perfect detection and omits sensor POD, false negatives, terrain, weather, and revisits.
The 5-hour and 50-hour results use one missing point and one parameter setting without confidence intervals or repeated scenarios.
Independent equal targets are summed without vessel-task assignment, collision avoidance, fairness constraints, or joint optimization.
The transfer exercise checks only a qualitative current direction and does not numerically recalibrate or validate the full pipeline.
Sensitivity varies only the search interval by plus or minus 10 percent and does not test other influential parameters or recommendation rank reversals.
The government memo omits key uncertainty, search-probability, and detection caveats, and its equipment table gives no currency or unit.
Data, references, code, software environment, random seeds, and expected outputs are not embedded as a replayable bundle.
A repeated footer numeral or watermark artifact is not part of the paper's logical page numbering and must not be inventoried as content.

Three focused JPEGs cover tasks, assumptions, current forecasting, trajectory physics, equipment optimization, grid search, Bayesian updates, transfer, sensitivity, and the complete memo.
